models_evaluated: ChatGPT-RAG (GPT-4o-mini with retrieval grounded in TED literature)

links.outcome: Clinical quality ratings of RAG-grounded chatbot versus ungrounded general-purpose chatbot on TED questions
links.effect: ChatGPT-RAG mean clinical score 5.55 vs ChatGPT 4.94 (implied); OpenEvidence 5.96 outperformed both ChatGPT and ChatGPT-RAG (g = 0.53, P < 0.001). RAG was intermediate on clinical and non-clinical metrics.
links.quote: Across both domains, ChatGPT-RAG achieved intermediate performance, more closely trailing OpenEvidence clinically (g = 0.53) and ChatGPT with respect to non-clinical metrics (g = 0.44).

links.effect: ChatGPT-RAG was intermediate, trailing OpenEvidence clinically (g=0.53) and ChatGPT on non-clinical metrics (g=0.44).
links.quote: Across both domains, ChatGPT-RAG achieved intermediate performance, more closely trailing OpenEvidence clinically (g = 0.53) and ChatGPT with respect to non-clinical metrics (g = 0.44).

links.effect: OpenEvidence clinical score 5.96 vs ChatGPT 4.94 (Hedges' g=1.21) and ChatGPT-RAG 5.55 (g=0.53), both P<0.001.
links.quote: OpenEvidence significantly outperformed both ChatGPT (mean clinical score 5.96 vs 4.94; Hedges' g = 1.21, P < 0.001) and ChatGPT-RAG (5.96 vs 5.55; g = 0.53, P < 0.001) in clinical rankings and across most clinical metrics, including accuracy and relevance.

links.effect: ChatGPT outperformed specialized models: 18.4 vs 14.96 for OpenEvidence; g=1.25, P<0.001.
links.quote: However, performance patterns reversed for non-clinical metrics, with ChatGPT consistently outperforming specialized models in empathy, understandability, and actionability (18.4 vs 14.96 for OpenEvidence; g = 1.25, P < 0.001).
